summary: Nebraska fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen after a fourth straight loss, and an angry Matt Rhule handed play-calling to Glenn Thomas. The Chiefs ruled out three defensive players for Sunday against the Jets and are working the phones for a receiver before Tuesday's trade deadline. In San Francisco, Daniel Lurie's charter-measure sweep hands him more power at City Hall in the same week his office fired most of its Bloomberg-funded innovation team. Bay Area voters passed a roughly $1 billion-a-year tax to save BART and Muni. And in New York, Sweden's Andreas Almgren won his marathon debut in 2:06:01.

items.title: 'Angry' Matt Rhule fires Nebraska OC Dana Holgorsen after 4th straight loss; Glenn Thomas takes over play-calling
items.subheader: Out less than a week after Rhule called him one of the best offensive minds of our generation. Glenn Thomas takes over play-calling for the final three games, starting with the fallout from Friday's 24-13 loss at Illinois.

quotes.text: Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed and I am frustrated with our results this season.
quotes.by: Matt Rhule, Nebraska head coach, in a statement

quotes.text: While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution is simply not working.

items.title: Illinois 24, Nebraska 13: Huskers drop 4th straight after a 5-0 start; Owen Chambliss injured
items.subheader: The loss in Champaign made Illinois bowl-eligible and cost Nebraska its offensive coordinator less than 24 hours later.

items.title: Glenn Thomas gets 3 games as Nebraska's play-caller to make his case for the full-time job
items.subheader: The co-OC and quarterbacks coach has worked under Rhule since Temple and Baylor, with prior OC stops at UNLV and Arizona State.
items.image_alt: Illustration of a coach holding a play-call sheet on the sideline (generated)

quotes.text: Co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas will take over play-calling duties.

items.title: Holgorsen pays the price for Nebraska's skid for now; Rhule's expensive buyout is the real question in Lincoln
items.subheader: Rhule stays on the hot seat after the intermediate move and says more changes will come where they help the program win.
items.image_alt: Matt Rhule on the Nebraska sideline, via Getty/Heavy

quotes.text: I will continue to evaluate our program through the season and certainly at its conclusion and make additional changes where I believe they will help us win.

items.title: Chiefs rule out CB Mansoor Delane, DTs Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott vs. Jets; Mahomes, Kelce, Rice expected to play
items.subheader: CB Mansoor Delane and DTs Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott are out; Mahomes, Kelce and Rashee Rice are expected to play. The Jets lose Garrett Wilson. KC elevated defensive line help from the practice squad.

items.title: Chiefs among teams calling on WRs ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, per Rapoport and Schefter; Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs, Calvin Ridley linked
items.subheader: Rapoport and Schefter both have KC among the teams calling. Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs and Calvin Ridley are the names in play; the Colts reportedly already hold a fourth-round offer for Downs.

items.title: Andreas Almgren wins NYC Marathon debut in 2:06:01; Chepkirui regains women's title
items.subheader: The Swede ran 2:06:01, breaking away from Yeman Crippa late. He picked New York because position matters more than the clock there. Chepkirui regained the women's title.

quotes.text: I didn't really look at my watch or the time or try to calculate a finishing time or anything. I just tried to stay up in the front then see what happened.
quotes.by: Andreas Almgren, at the post-race press conference

quotes.text: It would have been nice to have a 2:05 time, but I'm very happy about the win.

items.image_alt: Andreas Almgren at the 2026 NYC Marathon, via World Athletics

items.title: SF got $7M to expand its innovation team. Lurie just fired most of it
items.subheader: Six of 10 staffers were fired Friday with no severance. City Hall won't say whether it met the conditions on Bloomberg's largest-ever city innovation grant, including a $2.38M payment due Nov. 1.

quotes.by: Mayor's office statement, which did not dispute that six of 10 staffers lost their jobs

quotes.text: With that technology becoming more capable than it was even a couple of years ago, the Mayor's Office of Innovation should be capable of tackling a wide range of challenges.

items.image_alt: SF Standard image for the innovation office story

items.title: SF voters pass Props D, E and F after $14M billionaire-backed campaign, handing Lurie sole power over department heads
items.subheader: Props D, E and F passed with roughly $14M in billionaire backing, handing the mayor more control over ballots, contracts and department heads. Analysts say the blame game ends here.

quotes.text: These charter reform measures will make it very hard now for mayors to argue credibly that they don't have the authority to do what voters ask of them.
quotes.by: Jason McDaniel, SFSU political science professor

quotes.text: He has all the power he asked for. Let's see what he does with it.
These victories are not a finish line, they are a starting point.
quotes.by: Daniel Lurie, in his victory speech Tuesday night

items.image_alt: Daniel Lurie at his election watch party, photo by Genesia Ting for Mission Local

items.title: Regional Transit Measure passes with 62% region-wide and 79% in SF; ~$1B/yr sales tax saves BART, Muni, Caltrain from 2027 cuts
items.subheader: The Regional Transit Measure, a sales tax worth roughly $1B a year for BART, Muni, Caltrain and AC Transit, won 62% region-wide and 79% in SF. Prop H's Muni parcel tax took 74%.

quotes.text: This is existential, especially for BART.
quotes.by: Tom Radulovich, former BART board member, before the vote
